method: Each section read in full by a machine-assisted reviewer against the packs and the ground catalogue as of this date; not a legal review.

sections.bearsOn: Establishes the two landscape units, shown on Maps 1 and 2, as the area the objectives apply to; no DataBC layer the planner reads draws them.

Requires openings and cutblocks in each unit to follow Table 1 (NDT 2: under 40 ha 30-40%, 40-80 ha 30-40%, 80-250 ha 20-40%; NDT 3: under 40 ha 10-20%, 40-250 ha 10-20%, 250-1000 ha 60-80%), so a block's size moves its unit's distribution.
sections.gapNote: The patch analysis runs the PG TSA Table 7 classes only; Obo-Fox Table 1 has its own classes (up to 1000 ha) split by NDT, and the unit boundaries are not in any layer the planner reads.
proposedFacts: Is the block in the Obo River or Fox landscape unit, and in NDT 2 or NDT 3?
After this block, what percent of the unit's openings fall in each Table 1 patch size class?
Does the block move any Table 1 class farther outside its range?

sections.bearsOn: Requires forested patches to be retained by Table 1's distribution to limit fragmentation; the same table as 1.A.a, read for leave areas.
sections.gapNote: Falls with a Table 1 patch test for 1.A.a.

sections.bearsOn: Lets the two largest classes run larger where the district manager considers it required for caribou, forest health or natural disturbance patterns.
sections.gapNote: A reviewer question on a Table 1 rule.

sections.bearsOn: Lets the district manager approve clustered cutblocks that together emulate patches of 40 ha or more, so several blocks may count as one patch.
sections.gapNote: A Table 1 rule would need to group approved clusters before classing patches.

sections.bearsOn: Lets the district manager approve short-term departures from the Table 1 targets for fire-damaged stands, forest health or other significant constraints, the usual route for salvage blocks.
sections.gapNote: No rule records a deviation approval beside a Table 1 result.
proposedFacts: Has the district manager approved a short-term deviation from the Table 1 patch size targets for this block, for fire damage, forest health or another operational constraint?

sections.bearsOn: Requires each unit to hold Table 2's mature-plus-old and old percentages by zone (NDT 2 ESSF and SWB 42/13; NDT 3 BWBS 34/16, ESSF 34/21) and, where short, the old deficit to be mapped from non-early stands and reserved from harvest, which can take a block's stands out.
sections.gapNote: The old forest module calculates the PG TSA order only. The 2008 Mackenzie non-spatial order says it applies where it conflicts on old (it names 1.A.g and Table 2), so a rule would test mature-plus-old here and old under the 2008 order.
proposedFacts: What percent of each biogeoclimatic variant in the landscape unit is mature plus old, against Table 2?
Is any of the block in an area mapped and reserved to make up an old or mature-plus-old deficit?

sections.bearsOn: Asks that Table 2 targets be met where possible from areas already constrained for other values, which bears on where a deficit reserve may fall.
sections.gapNote: A reviewer note on any 1.A.f test.

sections.bearsOn: Lets BWBS retention vary as the Biodiversity Guidebook allows where deciduous stands predominate.
Asks that connectivity of important habitats be kept using areas already constrained from harvest; it names no measure a block can be tested against.

Requires every opening or cutblock to retain wildlife tree patches at the Table 3 percentage (3% to 18% of cutblock area, read from the unit's harvest history and the subzone's available share) unless operational plans detail retention that meets the unit's Table 3 targets.
sections.gapNote: The rule asks the reviewer to compare retention with the order’s Table 3; the planner does not read the table by subzone.

sections.bearsOn: Bars timber harvesting within 200 m (slope distance) of Weissener Lake (UTM NAD83 zone 10, 336161 E, 6403217 N) and requires 50% of basal area volume to be retained in a further 50 m.
sections.gapNote: The rule asks whether the block reaches within 250 m of Weissener Lake; no screen measures the slope distance.

sections.bearsOn: Lets the regional director (then MSRM) vary the no-harvest and managed distances for a specific area.
sections.gapNote: A reviewer question beside a 2.A.a rule; the approving office no longer exists under that name.

sections.bearsOn: Required forest development plans submitted after the effective date to be consistent; under FRPA the objectives reach a block through Land Act s. 93.8 and the FSP's results or strategies.
sections.gapNote: A document check that the FSP carries results or strategies for these objectives.
